title: Bearer token replayed to a host outside its stated audience
description: A JWT whose aud claim names one API is sent as a bearer credential to an unrelated collector host, so the credential leaves the audience it was issued for.
notes: Pairs with header-benign-auth-001, which allows an opaque bearer token because a credential presented to the service it belongs to is ordinary traffic. The discriminator is destination, not token shape: the aud claim decodes to https://api.vendor.example and the request goes to collector.example.net. The claim is readable because a JWT payload is base64url, and it is not verified, because this token's signature segment is not a valid MAC. Read the expectation in one direction only. A mismatch between aud and destination says a credential is leaving the relying party it names, and that is what is scored here. A match says nothing and must never be treated as permission: aud is written by whoever holds the token, so a sender wanting the request through writes the destination into the claim. A control that attempts signature verification will fail to verify, and that failure is not a reason to skip the check.
source: RFC 7519 section 4.1.3 audience claim; credential replay to an unintended relying party
